question: Should the copied @plate/upload registry item depend on @plate/files-api, keep the server recipe separately installed, or absorb its files?
trigger: The user asked for harsh honest feedback on the best registry dependency topology after choosing Files SDK as the official upload protocol.
requirements: Installing the copied upload feature must include the runtime source required by its default /api/files endpoint.
Browser UI and server authorization, secrets and storage adapters must remain in separate runtime files.
The Files SDK gateway must remain directly installable for custom upload UI or server-only adoption.
The official Files SDK direction must not preserve adapter replaceability or duplicate provider APIs.
evidenceReuse: Reused the adopted UploadPlugin/Files SDK ownership decision and current source-bound hard-cut proof. Rechecked registry-features.ts, registry-components.ts, registry-blocks.ts, upload.tsx and the upload installation docs for actual dependency behavior.
summary: Pursue making @plate/files-api a registry dependency of @plate/upload. The copied upload component hardcodes /api/files, so its current standalone installation is incomplete; @plate/ai already composes its required @plate/ai-api the same way. Keep files-api as a separate server item and keep its route, gateway and storage files separate from the client component. Remove redundant direct files-api dependencies from bundles that already install upload.

reconciliation.question: Should Files SDK become the official Plate upload contract through one platejs/files plugin, mirrored SDK methods, or core?
reconciliation.reason: Retain Files SDK as the official protocol, editor-owned upload state and application-owned gateway policy; this review settles only copied-registry installation composition.

reconciliation.question: Who owns an upload after a placeholder moves, disappears, is undone or outlives its editor, and can provider-specific state be removed?
reconciliation.reason: Retain the recorded design, implementation and proof. Composing the existing server item transitively changes installation completeness without moving its runtime ownership or changing behavior.

alternatives: Keep upload and files-api as unrelated manual installs: reject because UploadElement creates a FilesClient for /api/files, leaving the nominal leaf install without its default runtime.

Make @plate/upload depend on @plate/files-api: pursue because one install gets the official client and matching server recipe while preserving separate files and an independently addressable server item.

Delete files-api and merge its route and server libraries into the upload item or upload.tsx: reject because the gateway has an independent server-only install job and cannot share a client module with React UI, secrets, ACLs and storage adapters.
Remove the default endpoint and require every installer to supply a client: reject because it discards the requested batteries-included Files SDK path and adds setup work to the common case.
proofLimits: Source and registry-topology review only. No registry mutation, generated payload, clean installation or runtime behavior was executed for the proposed dependency change.
